limitations: Research observation only; not operation qualification.
Default Next bundler uses disposable source overlays; runtime observation is not production database qualification.
Selected SQLite reads use a disposable database; authentication and settings use fixture storage, not production persistence or the native database adapter.
OIDC uses a controlled private-loopback issuer, not external provider or account interoperability; redirect/session client transport is not established.
OIDC setup-completion catalog scheduling crosses a recorded fixture boundary; catalog revalidation is not executed or observed.
A2A status HTTP uses private SQLite settings and source cache, not native core; raw error text is not exported.

Combo metrics HTTP uses a fixture-only same-bundle owner seeder and inspector; normal requests execute the pinned handler. This observes controlled process state, not production chat, durable counters, other processes, an atomic lock or executor qualification.

Concurrency HTTP seeds one synthetic limiter and one slot in each semaphore through fixture controls; it executes source-extracted manager declarations and pause tracking, not body-update or provider-dispatch code, and does not establish production state, persistence, or concurrency races.

Auth status uses actual Next cookies, JOSE and pinned settings/cache declarations with a private disposable SQLite boundary; it is not native core lifecycle or optional executor credential qualification.
Well-known cards observe anonymous Next GET with no hub configured; hub failure, cache and projection behavior require separately bound handler tests.
Liveness observes only GET and HEAD on isolated Next with the pinned matcher and handler; it does not establish full application or production persistence behavior.

ACP uses the pinned handler, registry and manifest with a verified POSIX owned-executable boundary. A fixture Next server invokes pinned peer stamping on its accepted TCP connection; this is not the production custom server. Arbitrary production executables and Windows process behavior are not established. Source does not check request cancellation; a response cannot settle external effects.
Reasoning GET uses the pinned handler and store with an isolated query-specific SQLite fault and recovery; policy controls are separate and production persistence is not established.
Family policy uses exact method/path reachability controls with scoped tokens, not the pinned handlers, persistence, API-key scope alternatives, or executor safety.
Mapping ingress exercises policy with a reachability control at the exact method and path; it does not execute mapping handlers or cold database initialization.
Agent-skills ingress coverage observes management denial and a dashboard-session query, not every credential alternative or hosted failures.
Degradation handler failure was not induced; fixture signals control only the disposable in-process source registry.

The IP filter denial and recovery exercise forwarding-header fallback with unknown peer locality under bare Next start. They do not demonstrate authenticated peer-stamp denial, peer locality, or reverse-proxy trust.
